name: Robert's Ship
description: A turn-of-the-century polar expedition ship, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a stout wooden vessel with a distinctive rounded, egg-shaped reinforced hull painted dark blackish-brown, built to ride up over crushing sea ice, realistic weathered wood and paint texture. Three tall masts with furled canvas sails plus a single black steam smokestack amidships puffing grey smoke, a raised wooden bow. Sturdy and heavy-looking.

name: The Miranda
description: An older, worn wooden steamer-barque, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a weathered dark-hulled sailing ship with two masts, patched canvas sails, a thin black smokestack, and a visibly aged, ill-fated look with scuffed and stained planking, realistic weathered wood texture. Smaller and shabbier than Robert's Ship.

name: The Brass Sextant
description: A late-1800s French-made brass sextant navigation instrument, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a polished golden-brass triangular frame with a graduated arc scale along the bottom, a small sighting telescope, and mirrors. Compact handheld precision instrument, warm brass tones with a natural realistic metallic sheen and light reflection.

name: The Three Crates
description: Three large wooden shipping crates, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — sturdy pale-wood packing boxes with visible plank seams and dark iron corner brackets, bound with rope, of slightly different sizes stacked or set side by side, realistic wood grain and iron texture. Weathered but solid.

name: The Expedition Flag
description: A hand-sewn American flag, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — stars and stripes in red, white and blue fabric, mounted on a simple dark wooden pole, the cloth stitched and slightly worn as if homemade, realistic woven fabric texture catching the wind with natural folds.

name: The Wooden Sledge
description: A traditional Arctic dog sledge, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a long low sledge built from lashed wooden slats and curved runners, tied with rope and loaded with fur bundles, wooden boxes and coiled line, realistic weathered wood and fur texture. Rugged, functional, warm brown wood tones.

name: The Folding Boat
description: A small collapsible folding boat, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a lightweight canvas-and-wood-frame dinghy in tan and grey, narrow, shallow, and compact when folded, with a simple wooden paddle laid across it, realistic canvas and wood texture. Practical and worn.
